Brent crude was up 0.22% at $92.18 per barrel in early trade on Friday, well below its October levels above $110 but little changed from the start of the week, while WTI crude had gained 0.35% to $82.73 per barrel. analysis.summary: Crude prices are range-bound as agency forecasts of an upcoming supply glut offset ongoing Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy.

And Argentina’s energy export boom isn’t over. analysis.summary: Argentine energy firms are accelerating dollar bond sales ahead of the 2027 election amid strong Vaca Muerta output and export growth.

news.title: Norway’s Gas Sales Surge Nearly 20% as Europe Braces for Winter
news.summary: Norway’s daily gas sales jumped nearly 20% in October and were 5.6% above year-earlier levels. The rebound comes as the EU heads into winter with its gas storage facilities less than 70% full. Norway sold 11 billion cubic meters of natural gas in October, up 2.1 billion cubic meters from September, according to preliminary figures from the Norwegian Offshore Directorate. Daily sales averaged 355.6 million cubic meters, up from a revised 296.8 million in September and 2.2% above the regulator’s forecast. EU gas storage was 69.8% full…

analysis.summary: Norway's October natural gas sales jumped nearly 20% month-on-month and beat forecasts as EU gas storage sits below 70% entering winter.
analysis.rationale: The report covers European natural gas supply and storage without mentioning crude oil, providing insufficient textual evidence for a direct crude price impact.

news.title: China’s Oil Imports from Persian Gulf Jump to Wartime High
news.summary: China’s crude oil imports from the Persian Gulf surged by 42.4% in October from September, to the highest level since the Iran war began, as supply via the Strait of Hormuz rebounded and Gulf producers slashed prices for their crude to attract buyers amid record-high freight rates. China imported 19.7 million tons of crude oil from the Persian Gulf producers, excluding Iran, in October, a 42.4% jump from the previous month, per calculations by the South China Morning Post based on Chinese customs data released on Friday. analysis.summary: China's October crude imports from the Persian Gulf jumped 42.4% as Strait of Hormuz flows rebounded and Gulf producers cut prices.
analysis.rationale: Rebounding Strait of Hormuz supply and producer price discounts indicate bearish supply easing, while the sharp jump in Chinese import volume points to resilient buying demand.
